[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are various measures in place to prevent and punish corruption, including anti-corruption laws, independent anti-corruption agencies, codes of conduct, whistleblower protection, and transparency measures.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of independent anti-corruption agencies include the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) in Nigeria and the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) in India.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The effectiveness of anti-corruption measures varies depending on the context and level of implementation.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Enforcement of anti-corruption measures varies across countries; some have strong enforcement while others have weak enforcement.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The effectiveness of anti-corruption measures depends on political will, institutional capacity, and public support.  
[USER] User expressed frustration about corruption not being punished and wished for a way to ensure enforcement of measures.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To ensure enforcement, it is important to promote a culture of accountability, strengthen institutions, raise public awareness, encourage whistle-blowing, and promote international cooperation.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Eliminating corruption entirely may be challenging, but it is possible to reduce its prevalence through effective measures and good governance practices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Countries with strong governance systems tend to have lower levels of corruption.
